text:
Foam, foam



		Swallowing the sea, breathing blue water,
		cleansing with its salt the sick lungs
		of that tar of tedium that traps some
		beings who write to one another and bargain with death,
		and you must stand on the same ledge
		of stone, in the same crack
		of the glass, to understand.


		But they leave their reddened wake
		only for the others;
		for many of them there is no tragedy,
		only the desire to cut the final
		thread,
		to leave the world’s cage,
		only the last pulse, the fevered instant
		of unmasking her, of looking into her eyes.


		Only wanting to be a silent sea,
		the waves
		shearing off the thorns of anguish,
		giving the root of the voice
		to the cave of words;
		only to be a pill, a fortress of rest,
		dissolve consciousness,
		flood memory, be nothing.



		foam, foam
From the
		book The Song of the Lovers, Barcelona, 2006
